description: Use domain-specific language rooted in core business concepts. Responsibilities must form meaningful domain sentences. Mine vocabulary from stories, acceptance criteria, and domain discussions. Avoid generic terms (Hold, Get, Has), technical patterns (Manager, Service, Handler, Factory), and capability verbs (Exposes, Provides, Contains). Never leave collaborators empty—use a primitive type when no domain collaborator applies. Prefer domain concepts over primitive soup when multiple primitives form a cohesive concept.

do.description: Use concrete domain language that creates meaningful sentences

guidance.description: Define all collaborators for every responsibility. Use a primitive type (String, Number, Boolean, Date, Integer) when no domain collaborator can be used. Never leave collaborators empty.
example: Expires at date (or never): Date or null
Is valid at date: Boolean, Date
Defines discount (amount or percent): String, Number
Applies discount amount to order: Campaign
Is exhausted when fully redeemed: Boolean
(Every responsibility has at least one collaborator—domain object or primitive)

guidance.description: Create responsibilities that form domain sentences with specific meaning. Extract vocabulary from stories and discussions.
example: Expires at date (or never): Date or null
Is valid at date: Boolean, Date
Defines discount (amount or percent): String, Number
Applies discount amount to order: Campaign
Is exhausted when fully redeemed: Boolean
(Each responsibility reads as a domain sentence: 'Campaign is valid at date', 'Voucher is exhausted when fully redeemed')

guidance.description: Mine domain language from stories: size → defines voucher capacity; time frame → starts valid at, expires at, is valid at; code → is identified by code; validity → is valid at date
example: Instead of 'Hold time frame and validity':
Expires at date (or never): Date or null
Is valid at date: Boolean, Date
Applies discount amount to order: Campaign

guidance.description: Name concepts after what they represent in the domain, not technical patterns
example: Calculates total value with market prices: Money, Holding, MarketPrice
Evaluates risk score: RiskScore, RiskModel, Holding, MarketData
Calculates subtotal from items: Money, LineItem
Calculates shipping cost based on address: Money, ShippingAddress, ShippingMethod
(Concrete business concepts and domain verbs, not PortfolioManager or generic Get)

guidance.description: Use domain-specific collaborator types that have business meaning
example: Calculates subtotal from items: Money, LineItem
Calculates shipping cost by method: Money, ShippingAddress, ShippingMethod
Authorizes with payment gateway: AuthorizationCode, PaymentGateway
(Collaborators: Money, ShippingAddress, AuthorizationCode have domain meaning)

guidance.description: Think of whole behaviors over data. Prefer collaborators with other domain classes, not tons of primitives. When multiple primitives describe a cohesive concept, create a domain concept instead.
example: (Domain concepts as collaborators—Period, Discount, CampaignMetaDataCollection—instead of primitive soup)

guidance.description: Reference domain objects as collaborators, not as raw parameters in a list. When a concept (Customer, Campaign, etc.) participates in a responsibility, list it as a collaborator.
example: Records voucher code, customer identity, amount, timestamp: Voucher, Customer (CORRECT: Customer is collaborator)
Records voucher code, customer, amount, timestamp: Voucher (WRONG: 'customer' is raw - flattened into parameter list)
(Domain objects belong in collaborators, not as raw words in the responsibility text)

dont.description: Don't use Hold, Get, or Has as default—they are fallbacks that signal failure to find domain language. Don't leave collaborators empty. Avoid primitive soup (scattering primitives instead of domain concepts).

guidance.description: Don't leave collaborators empty. Use a primitive (String, Number, Boolean, Date, Integer) when no domain collaborator applies.
example: Campaign (CORRECT: primitives when no domain collaborator)
(Every responsibility must have at least one collaborator)

guidance.description: Don't use primitives that make up a concept—avoid primitive soup. Don't use Has, Get, Hold. Prefer domain concepts as collaborators over scattering String, Number, Boolean, Date across responsibilities.
example: Campaign (WRONG: primitive soup, Has, empty collaborators)
Is valid at date: Boolean, Date
Has voucher code generation parameters: VoucherCodeGenerationParameters
(Think whole behaviors—Period, Discount, CampaignMetaDataCollection—not tons of primitives)

guidance.description: Don't use Hold or Get. These are fallbacks when you cannot find actual domain language - and that is a sign of failure. Mine the domain first.
example: Hold time frame and validity: (WRONG: vague)
(Should be: Defines voucher capacity, Starts valid at date, Is valid at date - domain sentences)

guidance.description: Don't use Get as a substitute for Hold - it is equally vague. Find the actual responsibility.
example: Get code: (WRONG: what does 'get' mean in domain terms?)
(Should be: Is identified by code, Defines redemption limit - domain-specific)

guidance.description: Don't name concepts with suffixes like Manager, Service, Handler, Factory
example: (Should be: Portfolio with clear domain responsibilities)

guidance.description: Don't use capability verbs like Exposes, Provides, Contains, Represents
example: (Should be: Reports holdings, Calculates total value - specific domain actions)

guidance.description: Don't use generic terms like Data, Config, Parameter, Result without domain context
example: (Should be: Generates trades: Trade - domain action)

guidance.description: Don't describe system structure instead of behavior
example: (Should be: Payment - Authorizes with payment gateway: AuthorizationCode, PaymentGateway)

guidance.description: Don't use raw parameters for domain concepts. When Customer, Campaign, or another domain object participates, add it as a collaborator - don't flatten it into a parameter list.
example: Records voucher code, customer, amount, timestamp: Voucher (WRONG: customer is raw parameter)
(Should be: Records voucher code, customer identity, amount, timestamp: Voucher, Customer - Customer as collaborator)
